I've gathered enough evidence. Here's the summary of the investigation and findings.

## Investigation

Ran 8 cold launches of `dev.lincforge.benchtarget` on a real device (`<REDACTED-1>`), each time force-stopping and relaunching, then navigating Home → About → Diagnostics and inspecting the view hierarchy:

| Trial | Sync status | "Retry sync" button |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sync idle | visible |
| 2 | Sync idle | visible |
| 3 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |
| 4 | Sync idle | visible |
| 5 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |
| 6 | Sync idle | visible |
| 7 | Sync idle | visible |
| 8 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |

5/8 (~60%) idle-with-button, 3/8 (~40%) unavailable-without-button — matching the reported "passes about 3 out of 5 times."

## Root cause

The Diagnostics screen has a "Sync status" field that resolves on each cold start to either **"Sync idle"** or **"Sync unavailable"**. The "Retry sync" button is *conditionally composed* — it only renders when the status resolves to "Sync idle"; when it resolves to "Sync unavailable," the button node is entirely missing from the view hierarchy (not just disabled/invisible).

This resolution is non-deterministic per process launch: consecutive launches flip between the two states with no fixed pattern (idle, idle, unavailable, idle, unavailable, idle, idle, unavailable), ruling out simple alternation. It's also not explained by any observable environment signal — the status bar's WiFi/cellular indicators (full bars, AT&T, 100% battery) were identical across every trial, and the app's own About screen states "It has no network access, collects nothing," so this can't be a genuine connectivity check. That rules out real network flakiness as the cause.

**Conclusion:** the flake originates in-app, not in the test. On each cold start the Diagnostics screen computes a "Sync status" value non-deterministically (consistent with an unseeded random draw or a startup race between two async initializers), and the "Retry sync" button's visibility is gated on that value being "idle." The UI test asserting the button is visible is correctly observing real app behavior — it fails whenever that per-launch coin flip lands on "Sync unavailable," which happens ~40% of the time. Fixing this requires either making the app's Diagnostics init deterministic/seeded for tests, or having the test explicitly wait for and handle both sync-status outcomes rather than assuming the button is always present.
